reviewer: Codex static agent review; not human-adjudicated
rubric: full means the entire target entry is explicit or necessarily implied; partial means some target assertions are missing; missing means no determining policy; wrong means an explicit choice conflicts with the authoritative solution.

rows.evidence: R1 exports createAspect and AC1 also requests Aspect, although they are inconsistent in placement.
R1 specifies flattening and two unique underlying traits; first-occurrence order is unstated.
R1 rejects relations and overlapping schema fields.
R1 accepts tags with no schema fields and combines data schema.
R1 requires distinct IDs but does not specify numeric type.
No metadata immutability policy.
R2 includes add(aspect(data)) and bare default addition.
R2 has/get requires all, merges fields and omits tag data; zero merged fields imply an empty object.
Merged object/view does not establish shallow copying or aliasing.
No set behavior for incomplete entities.
R2 routes fields and preserves omitted values, but unknown-field treatment is absent.
No triggerChanged control.
R2 adds missing/default constituents and preserves existing data.
R2 removes constituents and leaves unrelated traits; missing-constituent removal policy is unstated.
R3 and AC3 cover all-present matching, trait/aspect composition and live membership.
R3 says merged aspect slot at parameter position; no skipped tag/Not slots or tag-only aspect slot.
R3 covers writeback and per-constituent changes but not top-level strict-inequality comparison.
No changeDetection never mode.
No non-never mode behavior.
No callback-destruction policy.
No notification-dispatch timing.
R4 and AC4 cover missing-at-least-one and membership updates.
R4 covers any changed constituent but does not explicitly require current completeness for Changed.
R4/AC4 specify transitions and spawn/incomplete cases but not tracking observation history.
Compose with Or does not specify constituent alternatives.
R5/AC5 cover completeness-gated subscriptions and callback entity.
R5/AC5 require unsubscribe to stop future callbacks.
No per-constituent versus per-operation callback count.
Distinct creation IDs do not explicitly require aspect-specific query-cache identity.
No multiple Not-group rule.
No mask-generation policy.
No function-schema behavior.
R6 requires correct behavior after reset.
R2 says notifications run for constituents whose data changes; solution uses ordinary setTraitForTrait notifications even when supplied recognized values compare equal.
